content: The text provided is a detailed and highly technical compilation of references, study methodologies, and findings related to the treatment of Neisseria gonorrhoeae (gonorrhea), Chlamydia trachomatis, and Treponema pallidum (syphilis). 1. The treatment of gonorrhea is increasingly complicated due to the rapid emergence of antimicrobial resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Resistance has been observed for all drugs previously used as first-line empirical treatments, leaving ceftriaxone, an extended-spectrum cephalosporin, as the last effective option in many countries. 2. The 2016 WHO guidelines for the treatment of gonorrhea were developed based on a systematic review of randomized and non-randomized studies. These guidelines emphasize the importance of monitoring antimicrobial susceptibility patterns to guide treatment decisions and prevent the development of untreatable gonococcal infections. 3. The systematic review included studies involving adults and adolescents with uncomplicated genital, anorectal, and pharyngeal gonococcal infections. The interventions evaluated included ceftriaxone (500 mg intramuscularly [IM] as a single dose), ceftriaxone (1 g IM as a single dose), and dual therapy regimens combining ceftriaxone with azithromycin. 4. Critical outcomes assessed in the studies included microbiological cure rates, adverse events, and patient compliance. Additional important outcomes included quality of life, HIV transmission and acquisition, and partner transmission rates. 5. The review also considered factors such as the acceptability, feasibility, equity, resource use, and patient values/preferences associated with the recommended treatments. These factors were evaluated to ensure the guidelines are practical and applicable across diverse healthcare settings. 6. Data collection for the review included searches of Ovid MEDLINE, CENTRAL, and Embase databases for studies published from 2015 to May 2021, with an update conducted in June 2022. A rapid search in August 2023 identified any new key studies that could impact the results. 7. The review identified 15 new studies reported in 17 articles, in addition to 41 studies included in the previous review. These studies provided evidence on the efficacy and safety of ceftriaxone, cefixime, and spectinomycin for the treatment of gonorrhea. 8. The GRADE approach was used to assess the quality of evidence and synthesize the results. Summary of findings tables were created to present the evidence for multiple treatment comparisons. 9. The studies included in the review demonstrated high microbiological cure rates with ceftriaxone-based regimens. Adverse events were generally mild and infrequent, supporting the continued use of ceftriaxone as a first-line treatment. 10. The review highlighted the need for ongoing surveillance of antimicrobial resistance in N. gonorrhoeae and the development of new treatment options to address the growing threat of multidrug-resistant gonorrhea. 11. Specific studies included in the review provided insights into the treatment of gonorrhea in various populations, including men who have sex with men (MSM), women, and adolescents. These studies also evaluated the effectiveness of different dosing regimens and combinations of antibiotics. 12. The findings underscore the importance of adherence to treatment guidelines to ensure optimal outcomes and prevent the spread of resistant strains of N. gonorrhoeae. Variability in prescriber adherence to guidelines was noted in some regions, highlighting the need for targeted interventions to improve compliance. 13. The review also identified gaps in the evidence, including limited data on patient values and preferences, cost-effectiveness, and feasibility of implementing the recommended treatments in resource-limited settings. 14. The WHO guidelines emphasize the importance of partner notification and testing for other sexually transmitted infections (STIs), including Chlamydia trachomatis and Treponema pallidum, as part of comprehensive STI management. 15. The studies reviewed included a range of designs, such as randomized controlled trials, non-randomized studies, and case series. The risk of bias was assessed for randomized trials, but not for case series included in pooled analyses. 16. The review process involved rigorous data extraction and verification to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the findings. The results were synthesized to provide evidence-based recommendations for the treatment of gonorrhea. 17. The updated WHO guidelines aim to provide clear and actionable recommendations for healthcare providers, policymakers, and public health officials to address the global challenge of gonorrhea and its associated complications.
